subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw add public lane-routing semantics for browser/workload/channel isolation, and should that be modeled as per-channel, per-agent, workload-classified, or priority-based scheduling?
rationale: This changes public config and core scheduler behavior for existing gateway deployments, so automation cannot safely choose the compatibility, resource-cap, and routing semantics.

options.title: Design a server-owned lane model
options.body: Add an explicit core scheduler design that owns lane classification, global caps, config schema, docs, and migration/doctor expectations before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to browser-only isolation
options.body: Implement a smaller browser workload lane if maintainers decide browser automation is the only supported special case for now.

options.title: Fold into broader scheduler tracking
options.body: Keep this issue as related evidence while using a broader scheduler issue as the canonical design vehicle for per-agent, priority, and workload isolation.

recommendation.title: Design a server-owned lane model
recommendation.body: Add an explicit core scheduler design that owns lane classification, global caps, config schema, docs, and migration/doctor expectations before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history points to steipete across gateway lane setup, agent runtime ownership, and scheduler docs.
